# 2. Database Model

PostgreSQL 17, schema managed by Alembic. Conventions:

* Primary keys are `uuid` (generated by the application). UUIDs are safe to
  create on any node and don't leak record counts.
* Every hotel-owned table has `hotel_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES hotels`, and
  every index that serves a query begins with `hotel_id`.
* Timestamps are `timestamptz` (UTC). **Stay dates are `date`** in the hotel's
  local calendar: a night belongs to a date, not an instant.
* Money is `numeric(14,2)` plus a `char(3)` ISO-4217 currency, never a float.
  Exchange rates are `numeric(18,8)`.
* Mutable aggregates carry `version integer` for optimistic locking, plus
  `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`.
* Translatable content (room type names, descriptions, facility texts) uses a
  `jsonb` **LocalizedText** value `{"en": "...", "fr": "...", "km": "..."}`.
  The UI falls back from the user's language to the hotel's default language,
  then to any available value. One column per translatable field keeps queries
  simple, and validation ensures that only supported language codes are stored.
* Extensions: `btree_gist` (exclusion constraints), `pg_trgm` (fuzzy search),
  `citext` (case-insensitive emails).

## 2.1 Entity map

```
organizations ─┬─< hotels ─┬─< buildings ─< floors
               │           ├─< room_types ─┬─< room_type_amenities >── amenities
               │           │               └─< rooms ─┬─< room_amenities
               │           │                          ├─< room_allocations (ledger, EXCLUDE)
               │           │                          └─< room_blocks
               │           ├─< facilities ─< facility media
               │           ├─< services
               │           ├─< tax_rates, currencies, exchange_rates
               │           ├─< rate_plans ─< daily_rates (room_type × date)
               │           ├─< pricing_rules, cancellation_policies
               │           ├─< guests
               │           ├─< reservations ─┬─< reservation_rooms ─< reservation_nights
               │           │                 ├─< reservation_guests
               │           │                 ├─< folio_charges
               │           │                 ├─< payments
               │           │                 ├─< invoices ─< invoice_lines
               │           │                 └─< reservation_events (history)
               │           ├─< housekeeping_tasks, room_status_history
               │           ├─< maintenance_requests ─< maintenance_comments
               │           ├─< channel_connections ─┬─< channel_room_mappings
               │           │                        ├─< channel_rate_mappings
               │           │                        ├─< channel_inbound_reservations
               │           │                        └─< channel_messages (log)
               │           ├─< document_sequences
               │           └─< notifications
               ├─< users ─┬─< user_hotel_roles >── roles ─< role_permissions
               │          ├─< user_sessions
               │          └─< login_events
               └─< roles
jobs, audit_logs, backup_runs, media_files  (cross-cutting)
```

| Table | Notes |

### Inventory and reservations (the integrity core)

| Table | Notes |
|-------|-------|
| `guests` | id, hotel_id, first_name, last_name, email citext, phone, phone_normalized, nationality, preferred_language, address…, date_of_birth, vip_level, tags text[], preferences jsonb, notes, id_document_type, id_document_number (encrypted bytea), id_document_country, id_document_expiry, marketing_consent, merged_into_id, version. Indexes: `gin (lower(last_name||' '||first_name) gin_trgm_ops)`, `(hotel_id, lower(email))`, `(hotel_id, phone_normalized)`. |
| `reservations` | id, hotel_id, code, booker_guest_id, status (`pending` \| `confirmed` \| `checked_in` \| `checked_out` \| `cancelled` \| `no_show`), source (`direct` \| `website` \| `booking_com` \| `agoda` \| `walk_in` \| `phone` \| `email` \| `other`), channel_connection_id, external_ref, arrival, departure, adults, children, currency, totals (accommodation, services, discount, tax, grand_total, paid, balance), is_overbooked, special_requests, internal_notes, cancelled_at, cancellation_reason, version. `UNIQUE(hotel_id, code)`, `UNIQUE(channel_connection_id, external_ref)`. |
| `reservation_rooms` | id, hotel_id, reservation_id, room_type_id, room_id NULL, rate_plan_id, arrival, departure, `stay daterange GENERATED ALWAYS AS (daterange(arrival, departure, '[)')) STORED`, adults, children, status, occupies_inventory bool, checked_in_at, checked_out_at. `CHECK(departure > arrival)`. GiST index on `(room_type_id, stay)`. |
| `reservation_nights` | (reservation_room_id, date), price, rate_plan_id, price_source. The nightly price is **fixed at booking time** and later rate changes don't reprice existing bookings. Basis for ADR/RevPAR. |
| `room_blocks` | id, hotel_id, room_id, start_date, end_date, reason (`maintenance` \| `out_of_service` \| `owner_use` \| `other`), maintenance_request_id, notes |
| **`room_allocations`** | id, hotel_id, room_id, `period daterange`, reservation_room_id UNIQUE NULL, room_block_id UNIQUE NULL, `CHECK (num_nonnulls(reservation_room_id, room_block_id) = 1)`, **`EXCLUDE USING gist (room_id WITH =, period WITH &&)`**. Maintained only by triggers on `reservation_rooms` and `room_blocks`. **This single constraint is what makes double-allocation physically impossible.** |
| `reservation_events` | id, hotel_id, reservation_id, at, user_id, source, action, diff jsonb. A complete modification history; the "Modified" badge is derived from it. |

**Status vs. "Modified".** `Modified` is not a lifecycle state: a confirmed
booking whose dates change is still confirmed. Modifications are recorded in
`reservation_events`, and the UI shows a *Modified* badge when any exist. This
keeps the lifecycle state machine unambiguous:

```
pending ──▶ confirmed ──▶ checked_in ──▶ checked_out
   │            │
   ├────────────┴──▶ cancelled
   └────────────────▶ no_show   (from confirmed too, after arrival date)
```

**Availability formula** for room type *T* on night *n*:

```
available(T, n) = |active rooms of type T not in room_allocations covering n|
                − |reservation_rooms of type T, unassigned, occupying, covering n|
```

### Pricing (implemented in phase 4)

| Table | Notes |
|-------|-------|
| `cancellation_policies` | id, hotel_id, code, name/description (LocalizedText), free_until_days (NULL = non-refundable), penalty_kind (`percent` \| `nights`), penalty_value, no_show_nights, is_active. FLEX and NONREF seeded. |
| `rate_plans` | id, hotel_id, code, name/description, meal_plan (`room_only` \| `breakfast` \| `half_board` \| `full_board` \| `all_inclusive`), is_refundable, cancellation_policy_id, parent_rate_plan_id + derive_mode (`percent` \| `amount` \| `amount_per_person`) + derive_value, room_type_ids[] (empty = all), valid_from/valid_to (stay dates), min/max_advance_days (booking window), is_default (exactly one per hotel, partial unique index), sort_order, is_active. A CHECK constraint keeps derivation fields consistent; cycles are refused by the service. |
| `daily_rates` | (rate_plan_id, room_type_id, date) PK, hotel_id, price NULL, min_stay, max_stay, closed (stop sell), closed_to_arrival, closed_to_departure. Rows exist only where something is set; clearing everything deletes the row. |
| `pricing_rules` | id, hotel_id, name, kind (`season` \| `weekday` \| `occupancy` \| `long_stay` \| `last_minute` \| `early_bird`), priority, date_from/date_to (nights), weekdays[] (0 = Monday), room_type_ids[], rate_plan_ids[], adjustment (`percent` \| `amount` \| `set`), value, conditions jsonb (`min_nights`, `max_days_before`, `min_days_before`, `min_occupancy`), is_active |
| `reservation_rooms.rate_plan_id`, `reservation_nights.rate_plan_id` | The plan that priced each stay and night. |

**Price resolution** (`app/modules/pricing/engine.py`, the only price calculator)
for plan *P*, category *T*, night *N*:

1. **Base rate.** An explicit `daily_rates.price` for (P, T, N) wins. Otherwise,
   if P derives from a parent plan, the parent's base rate is adjusted (percent,
   amount, or amount × guests, e.g. breakfast). Otherwise the room's or the
   category's base price is adjusted by the **rate rules** (season, weekday,
   occupancy) in priority order.
2. **Occupancy supplements** for guests above the standard occupancy.
3. **Discount rules** (long stay, last minute, early bird) on top of any price.
4. Rounded half-up to the currency's minor unit; never negative.

**Restrictions** come from the plan's grid row, or from the nearest parent's
row if the plan has none. Min/max stay and closed-to-arrival are read on the
arrival date, closed-to-departure on the departure date, and stop sell on every
night. Plan conditions (active, categories, validity, booking window) are also
checked. A booking that violates any of them is refused (`409`), unless a user
holding `reservations.override_restrictions` explicitly overrides it, which is
recorded in the reservation history. Staff date changes on existing bookings
are not blocked by restrictions; inventory checks still apply.

Nightly prices are fixed when booked: later rate, rule or plan changes never
reprice an existing night. Changing a stay's rate plan deliberately reprices
all its nights at current rates.

### Billing (implemented in phase 5)

One folio per reservation. Accommodation is **not** copied into charges: it
comes from the fixed nightly prices of the live stays (`reservation_nights`),
so there is a single source for room revenue. `billing/folio.py:recompute()`
is the only code that computes a reservation's money and is called by every
change (dates, rate, charges, payments, cancellation, check-out):

    grand_total = accommodation + charges (non-void) + exclusive taxes
    paid_total  = payments + deposits − refunds (non-void, in hotel currency)
    balance     = grand_total − paid_total   (> 0 owed, < 0 refund due)

Accommodation taxes are computed from the stays; service charges carry the tax
lines computed when they were posted (percentage taxes with `applies_to`
`services`/`all`); fees and adjustments are final amounts without tax.

| Table | Notes |
|-------|-------|
| `reservations.charges_total` | Sum of non-void folio charges (added in migration 0004). |
| `folio_charges` | id, hotel_id, reservation_id, reservation_room_id, kind (`service` \| `fee` \| `adjustment`), fee_type (`cancellation` \| `no_show` \| `early_departure` \| `late_checkout` \| `damage` \| `other`, fees only), service_id, name jsonb (service name in every language at posting time), description, service_date, quantity, unit_price, amount, tax_amount, tax_breakdown jsonb, is_void, void_reason, voided_at, voided_by, created_by. Only adjustments may be negative. |
| `payments` | id, hotel_id, reservation_id, number (receipt number, gapless), kind (`payment` \| `deposit` \| `refund`), method (`cash` \| `card` \| `bank_transfer` \| `online` \| `other`), amount + currency (as tendered), exchange_rate, amount_base (hotel currency), reference, card_brand, card_last4 (`^[0-9]{4}$`), notes, received_at, received_by, is_void, void_reason, voided_at, voided_by. **No full card number, CVV or track data is ever stored.** |
| `invoices` | id, hotel_id, reservation_id, number (gapless), status (`issued` \| `void`), issue_date, language, currency, bill_to jsonb, document jsonb (the complete localized, formatted invoice: hotel block, lines, taxes, payments, totals), subtotal, tax_total, total, paid_total, void_reason, voided_at, voided_by, created_by. At most one `issued` invoice per reservation (partial unique index); to correct one, void it and issue a new one. The PDF is rendered on demand from the stored snapshot. |
| `document_sequences` | (hotel_id, kind) PK, next_value. Kinds `reservation`, `invoice`, `receipt`. Incremented with an upsert that holds the row lock until commit: concurrent issuers queue, and a rolled-back transaction releases its number, so committed numbers are **gapless** (tested). |

Integrity: a trigger (`hms_guard_financial_row`) on `folio_charges`,
`payments` and `invoices` rejects any DELETE and any UPDATE other than voiding
(void fields, invoice status); a void can never be undone. Folio operations
lock the reservation row (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`) so concurrent postings from
several desks keep the totals exact (tested with parallel payments).

### Operations (implemented in phase 5)

| Table | Notes |
|-------|-------|
| `housekeeping_tasks` | id, hotel_id, room_id, task_date (hotel date), task_type (`departure` \| `stayover` \| `deep_clean` \| `touch_up` \| `inspection`), priority (`low` \| `normal` \| `high` \| `urgent`), status (`pending` \| `in_progress` \| `done` \| `inspected` \| `skipped`), source (`manual` \| `daily` \| `check_out` \| `room_move` \| `maintenance`), assigned_to, reservation_room_id, notes, skip_reason, started_at, completed_at, completed_by, inspected_at, inspected_by, created_by, version. `UNIQUE(room_id, task_date, task_type)`, so the daily preparation and automatic tasks are idempotent. |
| `room_status_changes` | Append-only history of `rooms.housekeeping_status`: room_id, from_status, to_status, cause (`manual` \| `check_out` \| `room_move` \| `task` \| `inspection` \| `maintenance`), task_id, user_id, at. Written by the single function that changes a room's cleaning status (`housekeeping/status.py:set_room_status`). |
| `maintenance_requests` | id, hotel_id, number (`MT-000001`, gapless), room_id NULL, facility_id NULL, location NULL (at least one required), category, priority, title, description, status (`reported` \| `in_progress` \| `on_hold` \| `completed` \| `cancelled`), assigned_to, reported_by, room_block_id (the out-of-service block it owns), started_at, completed_at, resolution, version |
| `maintenance_updates` | History and comments of a request: request_id, at, user_id, action (`reported` \| `status` \| `assigned` \| `edited` \| `out_of_service` \| `back_in_service` \| `comment`), comment, details jsonb |

The cleaning state is stored once (`rooms.housekeeping_status`: `clean` /
`dirty` / `in_progress` / `inspected`). *Occupied*, *arriving*, *out of
service* and *maintenance open* are derived on the room board from their own
sources (stays, room blocks, open requests) and never stored again.

Automatic work: check-out and in-house room moves mark the room dirty and
create a departure clean (high priority when a guest arrives in that room
today) and drop a pending stayover service; "Prepare today's list" creates
stayover services for staying guests and departure cleans for leaving guests
and dirty vacant rooms, skipping rooms out of service; completing a repair
marks the room dirty with a touch-up task.

Out of service: a maintenance request takes its room out of sale with a
`room_blocks` row (reason `maintenance`) created through the reservation
engine, so the allocation ledger refuses it while a guest occupies the room
and no booking can be placed on it. Releasing it ends the block tonight and
keeps the past nights as history.

### Restaurant & bar (point of sale)

| Table | Notes |
|-------|-------|
| `restaurant_outlets` | id, hotel_id, code, name (LocalizedText), kind (`restaurant` \| `bar` \| `cafe` \| `room_service` \| `other`), facility_id (optional link to the guest-facing facility), service_charge_percent, sort_order, is_active, version. A hotel without outlets simply does not show the module (except to managers, to set it up). |
| `menu_categories` | id, hotel_id, outlet_id, name, sort_order, is_active, version |
| `menu_items` | id, hotel_id, outlet_id, category_id, code, name, description (LocalizedText), price, station (`kitchen` \| `bar` \| `none`), is_available ("sold out" switch), sort_order, is_active, version |
| `restaurant_tables` | id, hotel_id, outlet_id, label (`UNIQUE(outlet_id, label)`), area, seats, sort_order, is_active, version |
| `restaurant_orders` | The check: id, hotel_id, outlet_id, number (`CHK-000001`, gapless), business_date, table_id, order_type (`dine_in` \| `takeaway` \| `room_service`), covers, status (`open` \| `closed` \| `cancelled`), reservation_room_id (guest), discount kind/value/reason, subtotal, discount_total, service_charge, tax_total, tax_breakdown, total, paid_total, opened_by, closed_at/by, cancel_reason, version. Partial unique index: one open check per table. |
| `restaurant_order_lines` | Name and price copied from the menu when ordered; station; quantity; amount; notes; status (`new` → `sent` → `preparing` → `ready` → `served`, or `void` with reason); timestamps. |
| `restaurant_payments` | method (`cash` \| `card` \| `bank_transfer` \| `online` \| `other` \| `room_charge`), amount + currency + exchange_rate + amount_base, tendered (cash: change = tendered − amount), card brand/last 4, reservation_room_id + folio_charge_id for room charges, void fields. Append-only (same trigger as folio payments). |
| `breakfast_marks` | (reservation_room_id, day) PK, covers served, marked_by. |

Check money is computed in one place (`restaurant/service.py:recompute`):
subtotal → discount → service charge (outlet %) → food & beverage taxes
(`tax_rates.applies_to` `food_beverage` or `all`, percentage taxes, inclusive
or exclusive) → total. A room charge posts the whole check to the guest's
folio as a `folio_charges` row of kind `outlet` (net amount + the check's tax
lines), so the folio grows by exactly the check total and the invoice shows the
right taxes; it can only be voided from the check, which voids both together.
